steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a position paper arguing for an adaptive security architecture for digital healthcare in 6G networks. It should cover what 6G brings, the security and privacy needs of healthcare applications, what we propose, and how the rest of the paper is organized.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- What 6G is and what it adds
- Digital healthcare: latency and privacy requirements
- Edge processing, constrained IoMT devices, and our proposed adaptive security architecture
- Organization of the paper

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- What 6G is and what it adds
  - next-generation wireless; unprecedented speed, low latency (cite)
  - beyond evolutionary performance gains: convergence of computing, communication, sensing (cite)
  - better AI/ML integration; edge computing extended to local level (closer to UEs), operator and customer infrastructures
  - renewable energy sources inside/outside network; quantum computing/communication requirements
  - IMT-2030 recommendations (cite): AI and sensing, ubiquitous connectivity, integrated sensing; not in IMT-2020 (5G)
- Digital healthcare requirements
  - examples: decentralized clinical trials, mobile imaging, computer-assisted surgery, emergency response, telemedicine
  - low latency + stringent privacy set by regulators
  - IoMT devices monitor, process, store, transmit patient data
  - protect patient data under stricter regulatory/legislative privacy and security requirements (cite)
  - conventional IoT-cloud: latency, exposure to wider audience incl. potentially hostile nodes
- Edge processing and our proposal
  - processing at edge near source: lower communication cost, lower latency, efficiency, capacity
  - IoMT devices resource-constrained; can't run heavyweight security
  - need context-aware, resource-efficient, adaptable security for dynamic network conditions, resources, evolving threats
  - we propose adaptive security architecture: distributed ledger technologies, zero-trust (cite), differential privacy, federated learning
- Organization
  - Section 2 background/related work; Section 3 position statement
  - Section 4 evidence and reasoning; Section 5 counterarguments and rebuttals; Section 6 reflections

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
6G is the next generation of wireless communication technology, and it promises unprecedented speed and low latency. Besides evolutionary improvements in performance over its predecessors, 6G will also bring new innovations like the convergence of computing, communication, and sensing. 6G also supports better integration with AI/ML, because it makes it possible to extend edge computing to the local level (closer to UEs), and to traditional mobile operator and customer organizations' communication infrastructures. It also makes it easier to use renewable energy sources inside and outside the network infrastructure, and it is envisaged to support quantum computing/communication requirements. The IMT-2030 recommendations have new capabilities like artificial intelligence (AI) and sensing, ubiquitous connectivity, and integrated sensing, and these were not described in IMT-2020 (5G).

Digital healthcare applications, like decentralized clinical trials, mobile imaging, computer-assisted surgery, emergency response and telemedicine and many others, have considerable low-latency requirements and also strict privacy requirements that are set by regulatory authorities. In a digital healthcare solution, many connected things (IoMT) help with monitoring, processing, storing, and transmitting the patient's data. The patient's data has to be protected from possible exposure, in full compliance with stricter regulatory and legislative requirements for privacy and security. A conventional IoT-cloud setup has problems with latency and with exposing sensitive data to a wider audience, which may include hostile nodes.

- Edge processing and our proposal
  - processing at edge near source: lower communication cost, lower latency, efficiency, capacity
  - IoMT devices resource-constrained; can't run heavyweight security
  - need context-aware, resource-efficient, adaptable security for dynamic network conditions, resources, evolving threats
  - we propose adaptive security architecture: distributed ledger technologies, zero-trust (cite), differential privacy, federated learning
- Organization
  - Section 2 background/related work; Section 3 position statement
  - Section 4 evidence and reasoning; Section 5 counterarguments and rebuttals; Section 6 reflections

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
6G is the next generation of wireless communication technology, and it promises unprecedented speed and low latency. Besides evolutionary improvements in performance over its predecessors, 6G will also bring new innovations like the convergence of computing, communication, and sensing. 6G also supports better integration with AI/ML, because it makes it possible to extend edge computing to the local level (closer to UEs), and to traditional mobile operator and customer organizations' communication infrastructures. It also makes it easier to use renewable energy sources inside and outside the network infrastructure, and it is envisaged to support quantum computing/communication requirements. The IMT-2030 recommendations have new capabilities like artificial intelligence (AI) and sensing, ubiquitous connectivity, and integrated sensing, and these were not described in IMT-2020 (5G).

Digital healthcare applications, like decentralized clinical trials, mobile imaging, computer-assisted surgery, emergency response and telemedicine and many others, have considerable low-latency requirements and also strict privacy requirements that are set by regulatory authorities. In a digital healthcare solution, many connected things (IoMT) help with monitoring, processing, storing, and transmitting the patient's data. The patient's data has to be protected from possible exposure, in full compliance with stricter regulatory and legislative requirements for privacy and security. A conventional IoT-cloud setup has problems with latency and with exposing sensitive data to a wider audience, which may include hostile nodes.

Processing data at the network edge, near where the data comes from, can lower communication costs, reduce latency, improve efficiency, and increase system capacity for compute-intensive healthcare applications. But IoMT devices that are deployed in healthcare are usually resource-constrained and cannot sustain conventional heavyweight security solutions. So there is a need for a security architecture that is context-aware, resource-efficient and adaptable, and that protects sensitive information under dynamic network conditions, available resources, and an evolving threat landscape. In this research we propose an adaptive security architecture that uses potential emerging technologies like distributed ledger technologies, zero-trust security, differential privacy, and federated learning in a resource-constrained environment.

The rest of the paper is organized like this. Section 2 describes background and related work, and Section 3 gives our position statement. Section 4 gives evidence and reasoning to support our position, so that our arguments are grounded in fact and logic. Section 5 has counterarguments and rebuttals that address the opposing perspectives, and Section 6 reflects on the discussions in the article.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
6G is the next-generation wireless communication technology, promising unprecedented speed and low latency [1]. In addition to evolutionary improvements in performance over its predecessors, 6G will also include novel innovations such as the convergence of computing, communication, and sensing [2]. It also supports better integration with AI/ML by enabling the extension of edge computing to the local level (closer to UEs), as well as to traditional mobile operator and customer organizations' communication infrastructures. It also facilitates the use of renewable energy sources, within and outside the network infrastructure, and it is envisaged to support quantum computing/communication requirements. The IMT-2030 recommendations [1] comprise novel capabilities such as artificial intelligence (AI) and sensing, ubiquitous connectivity, and integrated sensing, which were not described in IMT-2020 (5G).

Digital healthcare applications, including decentralized clinical trials, mobile imaging, computer-assisted surgery, emergency response and telemedicine, among many others, have considerable low-latency and stringent privacy requirements governed by regulatory authorities. In a digital healthcare solution, numerous connected things (IoMT) help in monitoring, processing, storing, and transmitting the patient's data. The patient's data needs to be protected from potential exposure in full compliance with stricter regulatory and legislative requirements for privacy and security [3]. A conventional IoT-cloud setup faces the challenges of latency and of exposing sensitive data to a wider audience consisting of potentially hostile nodes.

Processing data at the network edge near the data source enables lower communication costs, reduced latency, enhanced efficiency, and increased system capacity for compute-intensive healthcare applications. However, IoMT devices deployed in healthcare scenarios are generally resource-constrained and unable to sustain conventional heavyweight security solutions. Hence, a context-aware and resource-efficient adaptable security architecture is needed to protect sensitive information under dynamic network conditions, available resources, and an evolving threat landscape. In this research, we propose an adaptive security architecture that leverages potential emerging technologies such as distributed ledger technologies, zero-trust [4] security, differential privacy, and federated learning in a resource-constrained environment.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows: Section 2 describes the background and related work, and Section 3 presents our position statement. Section 4 provides evidence and reasoning to support our position, ensuring our arguments are grounded in fact and logic. Section 5 comprises counterarguments and rebuttals addressing the opposing perspectives, and Section 6 reflects on the discussions presented in the article.

[2] Shen, S., Yu, C., Zhang, K., Ni, J., Ci, S.: Adaptive and dynamic security in ai-empowered 6g: From an energy efficiency perspective. IEEE Communications Standards Magazine 5 (3), 80–88 (2021). https://doi.org/10.1109/MCOMSTD.101.2000090
